figures.caption: FIGURE 6-31 Significant blood loss results in reduced stroke volume (SV). To compensate, the body increases heart rate (HR) and systemic vascular resistance to maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP).
figures.publisher_description: M A P equals C O times P V R. Mean or average B P equals Cardiac output times Peripheral vascular resistance. Cardiac output equals H R times S V, that is, 80 per minute times 70 milliliters per beat which is 5600 milliliters per minute or 5.6 liters per minute. Mean or average B P equals H R times S V times Peripheral vascular resistance. A massive hemorrhage reduces stroke volume. In order to maintain B P, Vascular resistance and H R must increase.

figures.caption: FIGURE 6-33 The basic configuration of the nervous system.
figures.publisher_description: At the top of the diagram is central nervous system or C N S with brain and spinal cord. Then comes the peripheral nervous system with nerves that connect all parts of the body to the brain and motor division, which is made up of motor fibers that conduct nerve impulses from C N S to muscles and glands. The motor division is divided into two, autonomic nervous system that conducts nerve impulses from C N S to organs and glands and the somatic nervous system that conducts nerve impulses from C N S to muscles; voluntary control. Then comes the sympathetic division that activates body during emergency situations and the parasympathetic division that controls nonemergency functions. The sensory division conducts sensory information from sense organs and other internal organs to C N S through the peripheral nervous system, which has nerves that connect all parts of the body to the brain, that is, the central nervous system or C N S with brain and spinal cord.
figures.depicts: A flowchart of nervous-system organization: the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) processing information from the body and commanding it to action, above the peripheral nervous system, which branches into the somatic nervous system controlling voluntary muscles and the autonomic nervous system splitting into parasympathetic (feed or breed) and sympathetic (fight or flight); no brain regions or lobes are labelled.
